text:
Aparna: Heads-up — since 07:02 we've seen ~40% preemption rate on the spot-gpu pool in us-west1. Autoscaler kept removing nodes then adding, lots of pod churn and evictions.
Jon: Confirmed. Batch inference latencies spiked ~3x and some jobs failed with node lost errors.
InfraBot: Alert: spot-pool-us-west1 preemptions=42% window=7m
Keiko: Is the on-demand fallback pool not kicking in? I thought we had a 2-node on-demand buffer per region.
Aparna: That's the weird bit — the on-demand nodes exist but model-serving pods aren't scheduling onto them. Logs show `taint "dedicated=ondemand:NoSchedule"` and our pods have nodeAffinity `gpu: spot-only`.
Jon: Right — affinity is required, so CA spun up on-demand but scheduler refused to place due to hard affinity. CA logs: `ScaleUp: 2 nodes (ondemand-gpu-us-west1) created; Pending pods still unschedulable due to NodeAffinity`
Keiko: Oof. Two quick options: change affinity to preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution, or add a toleration + remove the hard label for a subset of pods. Prefer the preferred route for minimal risk.
Aparna: Agreed. Also propose: 1) add toleration for `preemptible=true:NoSchedule` on model-serving so fallback can land, 2) add `preferred` affinity to prefer spot but allow ondemand, 3) bump CA minNodes for spot pool to keep warm nodes (reduce churn), 4) increase `scaleDownForbiddenDuration` to avoid immediate teardown during rebalancing.
Jon: Also consider CA expander strategy: switch from `lowest-price` to `priority` so ondemand fallback isn't penalized during mixed scaling. And enable `balance-similar-node-groups` = true to avoid cross-pool thrash.
Keiko: Cost trade-off: keeping 2 ondemand buffer nodes per region ~ +$12k/mo (est). But the cost of repeated cache-warm + tail latency (SLO breaches) is higher. I'll run precise numbers and include in the rerunbook.
Aparna: For immediate mitigation I'll patch deployments to add the toleration and change affinity to preferred. Rolling update starting now.
InfraBot: Deploy started by Aparna — rolling update model-serving-v2 (5 pods) — 07:10
Jon: Patch applied, scheduler now placing 3 pods onto ondemand nodes. Latency down to near baseline. Still seeing a couple of evictions during state transfer.
Keiko: Follow-ups: create a small KEP/runbook for spot fallback policy: include node-pool taints/tolerations, affinity patterns, CA sizing recommendations, and a cost/benefit calc. Also add a Grafana panel for `pod_unschedulable_due_to_affinity` and CA event spikes.
Aparna: Assigning runbook owners: Keiko + Jon. Keiko can own the cost analysis and runbook draft; Jon will handle CA config changes and tests.
Jon: I'll schedule a canary test in staging to validate preferredAffinity + toleration under forced preemption.
Keiko: I'll model monthly delta for buffers and a threshold for when we switch to more ondemand (e.g., >20% sustained preemptions for 15m).
Aparna: Thanks — great catch. If we see another spike, we should also consider node-protection windows on critical pods and a small stateful on-demand pool for large KV caches. :thumbsup:
